Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: transparent contour-only character illustration for a Chinese cultivation game's interactive meridian atlas.
Input image 1 is the EXISTING EDIT TARGET. Revise this exact three-headed six-armed Asura rather than inventing a different character.
User's main correction: the two rear heads must have DIFFERENT expressions and different head turns; the four rear arms must have different poses, and every hand must be anatomically identifiable as a LEFT or RIGHT hand. Prioritize clear anatomy over ornament.

Preserve: exactly THREE heads, SIX arms, SIX hands, TWO legs; the existing natural adult proportions, central head identity and topknot, muscular torso, waist wrap, legs and feet and standing pose, overall portrait framing and size. Keep central head, torso, waist and lower body as close to pixel-registered with reference as possible. Maintain the reference canvas aspect ratio, ideally exactly 1122 x 1402. All extremities fully inside canvas.

Change:
- Central head faces forward with restrained stern composure.
- Rear head on viewer LEFT turns outward and slightly DOWN, half-lidded eyes, compressed lips, cold calculating expression, visibly three-quarter face.
- Rear head on viewer RIGHT turns outward and slightly UP, brows sharply knitted, mouth slightly open with anger, a distinctly different three-quarter/profile angle. Make the different moods legible using only a few expressive contour strokes.
- The FRONT pair of arms remains closest to the viewer, anatomically continuous with the chest shoulders, reaching diagonally downward as in the reference. One relaxed hand and one naturally curled hand; keep hand positions near existing positions.
- The two REAR pairs fan from behind the shoulder girdle with clearly separated roots, upper arms, elbows, forearms, wrists, and hand silhouettes. Each pair must consist of one anatomical RIGHT hand on viewer-left and one anatomical LEFT hand on viewer-right; exactly three left hands and three right hands total. Clearly draw thumb attachment, thenar contour, palm vs dorsal knuckle plane, and foreshortened fingers. Do NOT rotate a wrist unnaturally or attach a hand backwards.
- Upper viewer-left rear arm: elbow bent, raised OPEN palm facing obliquely toward viewer, fingers relaxed and slightly spread (NOT the reference duplicated finger-ring mudra).
- Upper viewer-right rear arm: elbow at a different angle and slightly lower height, a loose fist seen mostly from the back, distinct readable thumb wrapping over the curled fingers, NOT a mirrored raised open palm.
- Middle viewer-left rear arm: extends out diagonally with palm turned UP in a relaxed cupped offering gesture.
- Middle viewer-right rear arm: extends a little more horizontally and forward with clear foreshortening, palm turned DOWN, fingers gently extended. Different elbow heights and forearm rotations on the two sides. Do not cross or cover the central torso.
Show the spatial layering through contours, natural wrist axes, shortening of farther limbs and selective occlusion. Keep negative space separating all six hands. Remove loose ribbons that cross hands or obscure wrist anatomy.

Style: same clean sparse fine monochrome dark-gray outline drawing, outer contours and essential internal anatomical lines only. NO color, NO shading, NO gradients, NO hatching, NO solid black masses. Hair and cloth only sparse contour strokes. All spaces between lines INCLUDING inside the figure remain TRANSPARENT. Genuine alpha PNG, no white fill, no opaque background. No text, labels, meridian nodes, weapons, extra figures, background, frame, symbols or watermark.

Edit the supplied transparent contour illustration. ONE local anatomical correction only: the raised OPEN HAND in the UPPER LEFT of the image has the wrong handedness. This is the character's anatomical RIGHT hand, with its PALM facing the viewer. Its THUMB MUST project on the IMAGE-LEFT / OUTER edge of this hand, and the LITTLE FINGER must be on the IMAGE-RIGHT / INNER edge toward the heads. Currently its thumb is on image-right, making it a left hand. Redraw ONLY that hand from the wrist upward as a natural RIGHT PALM: thumb low on the far left, then index, middle, ring, little proceeding left to right; exactly five digits; palm creases and thenar contour clearly indicate the right hand. Keep the same wrist position, raised-arm pose, hand scale, outline weight. Do not mirror the whole arm or image. Everything else MUST remain unchanged: all three faces and expressions, all five other hands, six arms, body, clothing, legs and feet, framing, canvas dimensions. Preserve sparse monochrome outline-only art and full alpha transparency inside and outside all contours. No color, shading, solid fill, background or text.
